jobs.jd: Porch Group is a leading vertical software and insurance platform and is positioned to be the best partner to help homebuyers move, maintain, and fully protect their homes. We offer differentiated products and services, with homeowners insurance at the center of this relationship. We differentiate and look to win in the massive and growing homeowners insurance opportunity by 1) providing the best services for homebuyers, 2) led by advantaged underwriting in insurance, 3) to protect the whole home. As a leader in the home services software-as-a-service (“SaaS”) space, we’ve built deep relationships with approximately 30 thousand companies that are key to the home-buying transaction, such as home inspectors, mortgage companies, and title companies. In 2020, Porch Group rang the Nasdaq bell and began trading under the ticker symbol PRCH. We are looking to build a truly great company and are JUST GETTING STARTED. You’ll partner closely with actuarial, product, and engineering teams to translate Porch’s unique property data into a durable competitive advantage in underwriting and pricing. jobs.jd:
At flaconi, we believe that diversity fuels creativity, innovation and growth. It thrives in all its forms of beauty. Our team is a mosaic of individuals from different backgrounds, cultures and life journeys, all united by a shared passion for beauty. Our commitment is grounded in our core values, particularly #trustinpeople. We hold ourselves accountable for creating an environment where every employee feels honestly valued, heard and empowered to contribute their unique perspectives to foster belonging.

flaconi is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes and encourages all qualified  from all backgrounds and identities, regardless of ethnicity, race, gender identity, migration background, national origin, disability status, sexual orientation, religion, or age to apply. 

If you require specific support during the application or interview process – e.g. live captions, more time for the interview or the task in a different format – just let us know so that we can adapt the process accordingly. We will do our best to make this possible.

We are seeking a (Senior) Data Scientist (all genders) to join a dynamic team of five within our DATA department. You'll dive into diverse challenges including training and deploying machine learning models, developing Generative AI and Agentic AI solutions, and statistical modeling. We believe in flat hierarchies, which means you'll work closely with colleagues of various seniorities in a fun environment. You'll play a key role in extracting valuable insights and developing data and AI solutions to optimize our e-commerce platform across Europe, taking end-to-end ownership of your projects and collaborating closely with business stakeholders along the way. Your contributions will have a direct impact on business decisions and process efficiency across a wide spectrum of unique use cases.

Your Role

  • Utilize time-series forecasting methods (e.g., ARIMA, LSTM, DeepAR, Prophet) for predictive modeling.
  • Conduct exploratory data analysis (EDA), advanced feature engineering, and dimensionality reduction (PCA, t-SNE).
  • Develop and implement deep learning models in PyTorch, TensorFlow, or Keras while leveraging transfer learning strategies.
  • Showcase your skills across key e-commerce data science use cases including demand forecasting, churn and CLTV modeling, pricing, customer segmentation, recommender systems, and personalization.
  • Handle large-scale datasets using distributed computing frameworks (Apache Spark) on a tech stack comprising Python (PySpark, pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, LightGBM), SQL, Databricks (Data Lakehouse & ML platform), AWS (S3, Lambda, EC2, SageMaker, Bedrock), GitHub, and AI-augmented tools (Claude, Copilot) while collaborating directly to proactively address stakeholder business needs.

Your Profile

  • Possess a strong grasp of core data science principles to select the most appropriate techniques, combined with advanced proficiency in SQL, Python (PySpark, scikit-learn, NumPy, matplotlib, pandas), and AI-augmented development tools (Claude, Copilot).

Your Role You will own data science workstreams end-to-end, serving as both a technical authority and a key driver for AI solution design. You will work directly with stakeholders to validate feasibility, design architectures, and deliver reliable, high-impact data and AI applications. What is it all about? Core Machine Learning & Time Series: Develop predictive models and feature engineering solutions, with a strong focus on time series, predictive analytics, and classical statistical inference. Applied AI & LLM Workflows: Build, evaluate, and deploy working LLM applications, including custom agents, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) over text and document data, API integration, and structured workflows. Prompt Engineering & Evaluation: Design robust prompts and establish structured testing methodologies to ensure LLM outputs are accurate, consistent, and reliable. Stakeholder Engagement: Work directly with technical and non-technical stakeholders to present findings clearly, translate business needs into technical solutions, and inform decisions through solid statistical reasoning. Experience: At least 5+ years of hands-on experience successfully delivering data science and machine learning projects end-to-end. Data Science & ML Core: Strong quantitative background with proficiency in statistical analysis (descriptive & inferential), time series, predictive modelling, feature engineering, and model validation. Applied AI Skills: Hands-on experience building LLM applications via APIs/connectors, implementing RAG architectures, prompt engineering, and building data-driven AI agents. Tech Stack & Cloud: High proficiency in Python. Experience with Azure (Azure AI Foundry, data stores), AWS (S3, Redshift for data retrieval), and familiarity with Microsoft Copilot Studio. Functional Capabilities: Strong critical thinking (validating both human and AI outputs), high autonomy, adaptability, and excellent stakeholder management skills. jobs.title: Data Scientist Geostatistiek en Bodemdata (Freelance)
jobs.jd: 📋 Taken en verantwoordelijkheden In deze rol ondersteun je de beleidsafdeling bij het uitvoeren en verfijnen van statistische analyses op bodemdata. Je werkt onder meer aan de volgende onderwerpen: Vlaams bodemkoolstofmonitoringsnetwerk Het Vlaamse bodemkoolstofmonitoringsnetwerk werd in juli 2021 opgestart. Over een periode van 10 jaar worden bodems onder alle landgebruiken bemonsterd, waaronder bodems in waterrijke gebieden, (half-)natuurlijke graslanden en bodems die worden beheerd door overheden, lokale besturen en burgers. Na drie werkjaren is veel data beschikbaar voor verdere statistische analyse. De resultaten moeten op termijn bruikbaar zijn voor LULUCF-rapporteringen en prognoses. Zo kunnen ze helpen onderbouwen of landbouwbodems of bodems in residentieel gebied koolstof opslaan of verliezen. Daarnaast brengen de analyses verbanden tussen verschillende bodemeigenschappen verder in kaart. Digital Soil Mapping Het monitoringnetwerk genereert puntdata over Vlaanderen. Om die data gebiedsdekkend te maken, combineer je puntdata met gebiedsdekkende predictoren via digital soil mapping en random forest. Een historische bodemdataset werd eerder op dezelfde manier verwerkt. Het is de bedoeling om die doorrekening te optimaliseren en af te stemmen op de verwerking van de monitoringdata. Europese Soil Monitoring Law De Europese Soil Monitoring Law is momenteel in onderhandeling. Als de wet wordt aangenomen, moet Vlaanderen verschillende aspecten van de monitoring van bodemdata statistisch uitklaren. Het gaat onder meer om het aantal monitoringplots, verbanden tussen verschillende methodes en de nauwkeurigheid, betrouwbaarheid en accuraatheid van de monitoring. Ook moeten monitoringseenheden worden uitgewerkt. Indicatoren en rapportering Je berekent indicatoren voor de opvolging van het Vlaamse bodembeleid en voor de voorbereiding van rapportering over de Europese Soil Monitoring Law. Je past bestaande methodieken toe, stuurt ze bij en werkt nieuwe methodieken uit in samenwerking met beleidsmedewerkers. Daarbij gebruik je statistische analyses, geostatistiek, datakwaliteitscontrole en machine learning. Je optimaliseert ook berekeningsmethoden. 📝 Jouw profiel Ervaring met het optimaliseren en tunen van databases en queries. Ervaring met digital soil mapping. Ervaring met het analyseren van datastromen. Ervaring met R. Ervaring met de publieke sector. Ervaring met databanken, in het bijzonder SQL en Oracle. Kennis van geostatistiek. Ervaring met machine learning. Ervaring met rapportering. Ervaring met scripting in Shell, Perl en Python. Vertrouwdheid met het domein bodem. ⚠️ Deze functie wordt aangeboden als een deeltijdse freelance rol (50%). Originally posted on Himalayas

jobs.title: Data Scientist, Phased Array Antenna System Validation
jobs.jd: Amazon LEO is an initiative to increase global broadband access through a constellation of 3,236 satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO). Its mission is to bring fast, affordable broadband to unserved and underserved communities around the world. Amazon Leo will help close the digital divide by delivering fast, affordable broadband to a wide range of customers, including consumers, businesses, government agencies, and other organizations operating in places without reliable connectivity. About this role We're looking for a Data Scientist to turn data from our satellite fleet into engineering decisions. Every satellite in orbit sends back a steady stream of telemetry. Every unit was also tested heavily on the ground before launch, and the ground segment watches the satellite every day while it operates. Your job is to connect these sources. You'll find out which in-orbit behaviors trace back to what we measured in the factory, which events repeat across the fleet, and which patterns point to weaknesses in the hardware design. Your findings will directly shape how we design, build, test, and operate the next generation of satellites. A typical problem starts small: a handful of satellites show a drifting temperature, an occasional link dropout, or a counter that creeps up faster than expected. You'll work out whether it's a real effect or noise, whether it's spreading, and what the affected units have in common. They might share a manufacturing lot, a configuration, an orbital environment, or a signature in their factory test history. From there you'll form a hypothesis about the physical cause and argue it in front of hardware, firmware, and reliability engineers who will push back hard. You'll also have to say plainly when the data rules your own idea out. Telemetry alone rarely settles the question, so your first stop is the ground test data we already have. Every unit in orbit has a detailed record from manufacturing and environmental testing, and the fleet as a whole is backed by an even larger population of units still on the ground. You'll dig through that history for the same behavior: did the affected units show early signs on the ground, did they sit near a test limit, does the effect appear across many units under certain conditions? Often the answer is already in data no one has looked at in this light. When it isn't, you'll design the ground experiments that can provide it. That means deciding which units to test and under what conditions, how many runs you need before the result means anything, and what outcome would confirm or refute the theory. You'll work with the engineers who run those tests, analyze the results, and close the question with a clear answer and a recommended action. Beyond individual investigations, you'll build the fleet-level view: baselines for healthy behavior, early warning indicators that catch emerging issues before they cause outages, and reliability estimates that tell us how the population is aging. You'll decide which recurring analyses should become automated monitoring and work with software engineers to make that happen. You'll be the person the team turns to when someone asks "is this normal?" about the fleet. The ideal candidate is curious about how hardware fails and comfortable with messy data from many sources. They can turn "we're seeing something odd on a few satellites" into a rigorous analysis and a clear recommendation. What you'll bring: - Master's degree or above in a quantitative field such as statistics, mathematics, data science, physics, electrical or aerospace engineering, or computer science, or PhD - 3/5+ years of hands-on experience in an applied or industry setting using Python and SQL to analyze large datasets such as time series, telemetry, sensor, or test data - Experience applying statistical methods (hypothesis testing, regression, time-series analysis, anomaly detection) to noisy, incomplete real-world data - Experience building visualizations and dashboards that communicate findings to engineers and decision makers - Experience framing and solving loosely defined problems, from the first question to a recommendation people act on - Ability to work with hardware and software engineers and turn their questions into analyses you can actually run Nice to have: - Experience analyzing telemetry from satellites, spacecraft, aircraft, vehicles, or other fleets of deployed hardware - Experience with reliability and failure analysis methods such as survival analysis, Weibull modeling, failure-mode analysis, and root-cause investigation - Familiarity with electronics or RF hardware, manufacturing test, environmental stress screening (thermal cycling, burn-in, HASS/HALT), or yield analysis - Experience with pattern-discovery techniques such as clustering, change-point detection, and unsupervised anomaly detection - Experience with large-scale data tools (Spark, Athena/Presto, Redshift) and AWS - Experience with visualization tools such as QuickSight, Tableau, Grafana, or Plotly/Dash - Experience working with software engineers on data pipelines: data requirements, schema design, data quality checks, and automating recurring analyses - Experience using AI-assisted tools to speed up analysis and automate repetitive work - A track record of changing engineering design or test decisions with data Export Control Requirement Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum. Key job responsibilities As a Data Scientist, you will… - Analyze in-orbit telemetry to measure the health and performance of satellite subsystems, and detect anomalies and slow degradation early - Correlate in-orbit behavior with pre-launch data, including manufacturing, production test, and environmental test results, to find which ground measurements predict on-orbit performance. This role turns that into accurate models that support our carrier partners and our growth, builds tuned models where they beat rules and off-the-shelf LLMs in claims (triage, intervention, return-to-work, fraud), and responsibly explores how data can help employees stay healthy through grape Care. jobs.title: Senior Backend & AI Engineer (Remote)
jobs.jd: This role is open only to candidates living in the EU or EEA. We can't consider applications from other locations. If you've built something before, start here The hardest part of a startup usually isn't the code. It's finding customers who really need what you build and getting them to change how they work. At Scalera, that part is done: manufacturers, suppliers and contractors across Switzerland, Austria and Germany already run their tenders through us every day. What we need now are people who can take the next unsolved problem and turn it into a product customers can't do without. If you've founded a company (whether it worked out or not), been the first engineer somewhere, or built something people paid for, this role was written for you. About Scalera Scalera is an ETH Zurich spin-off building AI for the €200B+ European construction industry. Large manufacturers and suppliers still run their most document-heavy processes by hand, from reading 300-page tenders to retyping purchase orders into their ERP. We automate them one by one. Our product matching already handles 1,400 tender positions in 16 minutes at 98% precision, work that used to take a sales rep most of a day. What you'll do You'll be part product manager, part engineer. You'll spend real time with customers and help shape what we build. Sometimes you'll spot the next problem yourself, and sometimes we'll hand you a clear priority to run with. Spend real time with customers. Join calls and site visits, sit with the people who do the work, and understand why they do it the way they do. You'll know their problems firsthand, not from a ticket. Shape what to build. Turn what you hear into a clear problem, a scope and a plan, and push back when the obvious request isn't the real need. When we bring you a priority, you'll own how it gets solved. Build it. Design and build backend services in Go and Python that turn messy tenders, catalogs and purchase orders into data customers can rely on. Ship, then check. Get it in front of customers fast, watch how they actually use it, and iterate. Own it in production. When something breaks at a customer, it's yours to understand and fix. Build with AI. Use AI heavily in how you work, and design systems that agents can use as well as people. What success looks like after 3 months There's a part of the product people now think of as yours, and you're the one deciding what happens to it next You've spotted a problem nobody asked you to solve, made the case for it, and shipped a first version You've shipped features from both sources: priorities we set and ideas from your own customer conversations At least once, you've talked us out of building something customers didn't really need You've left a part of the platform simpler than you found it You'll probably thrive here if You've taken something from zero to one: a company, a product line, or a side project with paying users You've built and run backend systems in production that other people depend on. We care more about your judgment than your language; you're strong in Go or Python and happy to work in both You're solid on data modeling, API design and messy real-world data You'd rather talk to a customer than wait for a spec You're comfortable with ambiguity. You can make progress while the problem is still half-defined, which at a startup it usually is You want a large scope of responsibility and are happy to own things well beyond your job title Rapidly changing requirements don't throw you. When customers or priorities shift, you adapt and keep going You enjoy direct customer contact and want to be on customer calls You make things simpler over time, not more clever You write clearly in English. German is a plus, not a requirement You probably won't enjoy it if You just want to code and go home You don't like talking to customers, whether on calls or on the occasional site visit Ambiguity and chaos bother you You want a well-defined backlog handed to you Your main goal is managing people soon. Here, scope grows with what you own, not with headcount Our stack Go and Python (FastAPI), PostgreSQL, GCP, and LLMs throughout the document pipeline. You don't need to know all of it on day one. How we hire Screening call (30 min) with our VP Engineering. It's two-way: ask us anything, including the hard questions. Technical deep-dive call : walk us through something you built from scratch, the decisions you made and what went wrong. Meet Scalera Day : join us remotely to work on a real problem with real (anonymized) construction documents, and meet the team. Offer : if it's a fit on both sides, we'll move quickly to an offer. Working at Scalera Remote within the EU or EEA Small team, no bureaucracy. You'll work directly with the CEO, CTO, VP Engineering and Customer Success Competitive compensation Founders and former founders: if you're unsure whether you fit, send a few lines about what you built and why you moved on. We read every one. Find Jobs in Switzerland on Arbeitnow

jobs.title: AI Systems Engineer | Agentic Platforms
jobs.jd: Position Overview We are looking for an experienced AI Engineer to join a growing Data Science & AI team focused on delivering innovative, enterprise-scale AI solutions. In this role, you will partner closely with business stakeholders to develop technologies that improve decision-making, increase operational efficiency, and generate measurable business impact. The ideal candidate combines deep technical expertise in artificial intelligence, machine learning, data science, and software engineering with a strong understanding of how to translate business needs into practical solutions. You will be involved throughout the full lifecycle of AI development, from requirements gathering and data preparation to prompt engineering, agent-based system design, deployment, and production optimization. This position offers the opportunity to help shape the future direction of AI capabilities across the organization while promoting best practices and contributing to the development of new AI-powered products and solutions. What Success Looks Like Successful candidates are comfortable collaborating directly with business users while building scalable, production-ready AI applications. You bring strong analytical and problem-solving skills, thrive in fast-moving environments, and balance speed with quality. You are naturally curious, innovative in your approach, and motivated by solving complex challenges with practical, high-impact solutions. Key Responsibilities AI Solution Development Design, develop, fine-tune, and deploy AI models and agentic applications that address a wide range of business needs. Build scalable AI solutions that can be effectively deployed and maintained in production environments. Business Partnership & Stakeholder Engagement Collaborate with business teams to understand objectives, gather requirements, and translate needs into technical solutions. Clearly communicate methodologies, recommendations, and results to both technical and non-technical audiences. Model Evaluation & Performance Optimization Establish and implement best practices for evaluating AI applications, including accuracy, latency, scalability, reliability, and cost efficiency. Continuously monitor and optimize deployed solutions to maximize performance and business value. Data Engineering & Preparation Develop and maintain robust data pipelines to support model training and inference. Ensure data quality and availability through effective preprocessing, labeling, and validation processes. Research & Innovation Stay current with advancements in artificial intelligence, machine learning, and large language models. Evaluate emerging tools, frameworks, and techniques to drive continuous improvement and innovation. Mentorship & Knowledge Sharing Support and mentor junior engineers and data scientists. Contribute to internal learning initiatives and promote AI engineering best practices across teams. Technical Requirements Required Experience AI Engineering Advanced Python development skills for both AI/ML applications and backend web-based systems. Agentic AI Systems Experience designing and deploying AI agents capable of reasoning, planning, and executing complex workflows with minimal human intervention. Experience implementing infrastructure-as-code solutions using tools such as Terraform. Our backers include Matt Schlicht (founder of Moltbook), the founders of Crunchbase and Republic, and VCs including Draper, Precursor, and Liquid2. We're working at the frontier of autonomous systems, building agents that don't just chat, but run entire businesses. Our system identifies business opportunities through market signals, validates ideas with live ad tests, builds and launches software products, and brings in human experts wherever agents fall short. That loop already runs end to end: from idea to launched product to first revenue. Over the next 12 months, our focus is on reliability, throughput, and self-improvement, making every launch better than the last. You'll lead the technical direction of the platform, building multi-agent orchestration systems, self-improving agent harnesses, and AI-powered backend services. This is a highly technical leadership role that combines architectural decision-making with hands-on engineering. Working at the intersection of Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning and Industrial Analytics, you will analyse manufacturing data to uncover patterns, identify root causes and drive process improvements. Your insights will support smarter decisions, enhance product quality and increase operational efficiency across manufacturing environments. You will develop and validate AI/ML models and advanced analytics solutions for use cases such as: Quality improvement and process optimization Anomaly detection and root cause analysis Predictive maintenance and failure prediction Productivity and yield improvement Process stability monitoring Decision support for engineering and manufacturing teams As part of a multidisciplinary team, you will collaborate closely with Process Experts, Technology Development Engineers, Data Analysts, MES/PLC specialists, Data Engineers, MLOps teams, IT professionals and business stakeholders to ensure solutions are scalable, explainable and aligned with real operational needs. You will contribute throughout the entire solution lifecycle, from problem definition and data exploration to model development, validation, deployment support and continuous improvement. Experience Experience developing Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence or Advanced Analytics solutions. Hands-on experience working with complex datasets in industrial, engineering, manufacturing or technical environments. Experience contributing to end-to-end data science projects, including data preparation, model development, validation and deployment. Experience with hypothesis testing, regression analysis, statistical significance and data interpretation. Experience with data science and machine learning libraries such as Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn, SciPy, Matplotlib, Seaborn, Plotly, PyTorch or TensorFlow. Familiarity with Git and collaborative software development practices. 4. MLOps & Industrial Deployment Understanding of MLOps concepts, including model versioning, testing, reproducibility, CI/CD and monitoring. Experience with cloud-based AI platforms, preferably Databricks, is an advantage. Knowledge of APIs, containers and deployment concepts is beneficial. 5. jobs.title: Senior AI Engineer
jobs.jd: OUR VISION EQUS is building the trust infrastructure for personal AI. Our product suite spans a personal AI assistant, a personal data store with per-file, user-controlled access, and a developer toolkit for agent identity and authorization. It all runs on a single permission rail designed around one principle: your data belongs to you. We are preparing for a major public launch and scaling from build mode to operate-at-scale mode. WHAT YOU WILL DO As a Senior AI Engineer at EQUS, you own the AI assistant layer end to end: architecture, standards, and the service contracts that security, storage and front-end engineers support. You are a technical decision-maker, not only an implementer. You recommend the right approach for each problem, and you are prepared to say "this does not need AI" when it doesn’t. Privacy, safety, and cost sit at the center of every call you make. Your day-to-day includes, but is not limited to: AI architecture and context engineering. Design the context augmentation pipelines, spanning vector RAG, CAG, agentic file exploration, Text-to-SQL, knowledge graphs, fine-tuning, and MCP-based context engineering, and select the right approach for each use case. Select chunking strategy, embedding models, and retrieval architecture for user-owned document systems with multi-tenant isolation. Privacy and security guides each decision. LLM integration and agent systems. Integrate and manage commercial and open-source LLM APIs, and deploy multi-agent systems with LangChain, LlamaIndex, or LangGraph. Lead model selection, prompt engineering, fine-tuning, and production evaluation across the AI stack. Evaluation and optimization. Build evaluation frameworks that measure output quality, relevance, and safety. Optimize pipelines for latency, token cost, and throughput, monitor production for drift and regression, and close the feedback loop from evals back into iteration. Privacy and safety engineering. Privacy is our product, not a compliance checkbox. Own PII handling, GDPR and CCPA compliance, encryption at rest and in transit, and user-scoped access boundaries at the systems level. Build prompt injection defenses, output filtering, and data leakage prevention, and partner with security and trust experts on agentic workflow guardrails and shadow AI detection. Infrastructure and standards. Deploy and operate production AI systems on AWS, Docker and Kubernetes, and GitLab. Define the AI service contracts and APIs other engineers build on top of, and set the standard for how AI works here, including mentoring engineers and raising the technical bar around you. WHAT YOU WILL NEED TO SUCCEED You have shipped AI in production, you know where pipelines break, and you make architectural decisions that prove right. You exercise strong judgment on build vs. buy and on what separates an MVP from a production system, and you know the cost-performance tradeoffs cold: when a smaller fine-tuned model outperforms a general-purpose large one, and when expanding the context window beats RAG. You treat AI safety as a first-class engineering concern rather than a review-stage checklist. As part of the new generation of AI-native developers, you have already been using Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, or a comparable tools as a core part of your development workflow and utilize processes that enable speed and efficiency without compromising code quality and human intellectual control over the deliverables. You have experience in both small and large teams, effectively use tools such as Jira and Confluence, and are a valuable colleague to product managers as new features and products are emerging. You have experience working effectively with consultants and outsourced development teams, including transitioning responsibilities for systems. YOUR EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE This is a senior individual-contributor role with some peer technical leadership tasks. A relevant degree in computer science or engineering is preferred but highly qualified individuals with demonstrated experience shipping AI products at scale are welcome. jobs.title: Data Engineer II, Alexa AI - ML Engineering
jobs.jd: Join Alexa AI - ML Engineering and help power personalized, proactive experiences for hundreds of millions of Alexa customers worldwide. As a Data Engineer II, you will design and own the large-scale data pipelines that turn raw customer-interaction signals into the context and features our personalization and proactive-agent models depend on, working side-by-side with SDEs to shape our data strategy and architecture. - You will build and operate ETL/ELT pipelines processing billions of records a day, using AWS big-data services (Glue, EMR, Kinesis, Redshift, DynamoDB) and distributed compute. - You will partner with SDEs and applied scientists to define data strategy, contracts, and feature pipelines, and to decide architecture direction together. - You will own operational health: data migrations, schema/platform updates, and triage of pipeline tickets, directly supporting the SDE team's work. - This is a high-visibility role: the data you deliver, and keep running, directly shapes what Alexa proactively tells customers, and when. Key job responsibilities 1. Partner closely with SDEs to help define data strategy, architecture direction, and the long-term roadmap for the team's data platform. 2. Design, build, and own ETL/ELT pipelines that ingest, transform, and load customer-interaction and context data at a scale of billions of records per day. 3. Own operational items end-to-end: data migrations, schema and platform updates, and triage/resolution of data-pipeline tickets, providing day-to-day support to the SDE team. 4. Partner with applied scientists and ML engineers to define data contracts, feature pipelines, and data-quality checks feeding personalization and proactive-agent models. 5. Operate and continuously improve production pipelines: optimize data delivery, redesign for scalability, manage deployments, and drive root-cause fixes for pipeline incidents. 6. Establish and document best practices for data modeling, warehousing, and pipeline design across the team. A day in the life You'll join SDEs in a design discussion to shape data strategy and architecture, then pick up a migration or platform-update ticket and see it through to resolution. You'll trace a data-quality issue in a personalization feature pipeline, support SDEs with any operational asks on your pipelines, and monitor the health of systems processing billions of daily customer-interaction events. You'll partner with applied scientists to onboard new signal sources and triage pipeline alerts. About the team Alexa AI - ML Engineering builds the personalization and proactive-intelligence systems that let Alexa anticipate what customers need before they ask. Data Engineers work side-by-side with SDEs and applied scientists, combining data strategy and large-scale engineering to turn billions of daily customer-interaction signals into the context, features, and content that drive Alexa's ranking, personalization, and proactive-agent experiences. We value ownership, data quality, and working backwards from the customer. - 3+ years of data engineering experience - 4+ years of SQL experience - Experience with data modeling, warehousing and building ETL pipelines - Experience with AWS technologies like Redshift, S3, AWS Glue, EMR, Kinesis, FireHose, Lambda, and IAM roles and permissions - Experience with non-relational databases / data stores (object storage, document or key-value stores, graph databases, column-family databases) Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. jobs.title: Data Scientist
jobs.jd:
Data Scientist | Semiconductor Metrology
Abingdon, UK

Reward and Benefits

  • £42,000 - £55,000 (depending on experience)
  • Annual bonus, 3x salary death in service benefit and private health care BUPA, EMI Share scheme.

If you are a Data Scientist who enjoys turning instrument data into proof of what is possible, why not join us in Abingdon, Oxfordshire, and help prove the analysis methods behind advanced semiconductor metrology systems.

We are looking for an ambitious and adaptable Data Scientist to join our new Data Science team in the Technology department, reporting to the Data Science Lead and working closely with our Modelling Scientist. You will generate and curate data, develop and test new algorithms, and benchmark them against what the instrument can physically deliver. When a method proves itself, you will package it for the Data Analysis team in Engineering, who turn it into robust product software. You will work with real customer use cases and wafer data from Applications Development, and proof-of-concept data from R&D.

We are an AI-first team, so you will use AI tools every day, while checking carefully what they produce. If your passion is speed, evidence and finding out what the data can really tell you, we’d love to hear from you.

What you’ll be doing

  • Generate synthetic data, and build and maintain the demo and performance data libraries
  • Analyse instrument data to quantify noise and limitations, and help establish the information limit, meaning what is physically extractable from the instrument
  • Develop and test new algorithms and analysis methods (for example PCA, percentile methods and machine learning) on real and synthetic data
  • Benchmark methods against the information limit: achievable performance, measurement uncertainty, gauge R&R and drift contributors
  • Write clean, reproducible prototype code with test data and expected performance, ready to hand over to Data Analysis, and build analysis tools used across the Technology department
  • Use AI tools every day to code, explore, analyse and report faster, verify what they produce, and present your results to the team

Education and experience

  • Degree or above in Physics, Data Science, Applied Mathematics, Engineering or a similar subject, or [2] years’ relevant experience in data science or quantitative research

Skills and experience we’re looking for:

  • Data analysis in Python (NumPy, SciPy, pandas, scikit-learn or similar)
  • Heavy, day-to-day use of AI tools in your technical work, such as coding assistants and LLMs, with the judgement to verify their outputs
  • Image or signal processing, ideally on data from scientific instruments
  • Statistics applied to measurement data: uncertainty, repeatability, noise and drift
  • Machine learning methods, and how to validate them properly
  • Clear, reproducible code and reports
  • Explaining results to technical and non-technical colleagues
  • Curious and adaptable, happy to work quickly and test ideas against the evidence

We’d love to see:

  • Atomic Force Microscopy or other nano-characterisation (SEM, FIB, profilometry), or semiconductor metrology
  • Physics-based modelling or simulation
  • Version control (Git) and C#, and experience building agentic or AI-assisted analysis workflows

A bit about us: 

Infinitesima is a privately owned company founded in 2001, as a spin-out of the University of Bristol, by CTO Professor Andrew Humphris. Our dynamic team of scientists and engineers is focussed on enabling the next generation of semiconductor devices through delivery of innovative products to customers around the world. 

Our strength lies in the varied perspectives that come from different cultures, experiences, and identities. We believe that true innovation is fuelled by collaboration, locally and globally. We strive to foster an environment where everyone can contribute meaningfully and thrive. If you require adjustments to take part in the recruitment process, please let us know, we’ll do our best to support you.

Your recruitment journey:

We will interview you: Monday to Friday UK Time 9am to 4.30pm and we'll be as flexible as we can with Global Scheduling

1st stage: (45 minute) Remote meeting to evaluate your experience and technical ability

2nd stage: (2.5 hours) Face to face onsite evaluating technical, presentation and communication skills along with your ways of working and your opportunity to to know more about us

If you're not comfortable with eye contact, let us know at the start of your interview and if REMOTE, once we've said hello, feel free to turn your camera off until the end.

We dress casually so informal attire is absolutely fine for onsite interviews. We want you to feel comfortable when you meet us and if there's anything else we can do to support your journey,

jobs.jd:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The role:

In Token Factory analytics there is no split into product analysts, ML engineers and data engineers. Each person owns a question end to end: builds the data, runs the analysis, and comes back with a recommendation that changes a decision.

Your responsibilities will include:

- Define core product and business metrics and build a single source of truth that Product, Finance, and Sales can rely on.
- Build a comprehensive view of self-service customers, including usage patterns, customer health, satisfaction, retention risks, unmet needs, and growth opportunities.
- Translate customer demand and commercial plans into capacity forecasts and support capacity allocation decisions.
- Measure effective capacity utilization and identify opportunities to improve the commercial value of available capacity.
- Develop and evaluate pricing and packaging models, including guaranteed capacity, on-demand pricing, commitments, clawback mechanisms, and provisioned throughput units.
- Provide data-driven recommendations for the self-service and managed offerings, including customer segmentation, pricing, and capacity.
- Partner with Product, Engineering, Applied AI, Finance, and Sales to turn insights into concrete product and operational improvements.

We expect you to have:

- 5+ years of experience in analytics or data science.
- Strong Python, SQL, and statistics: you understand the code and the methods you use.
- Hands-on experience analysing large-scale customer, product, and usage datasets using statistical / analytical or distributed data-processing tools.
- AI-assisted coding as your default way of working: you guide it, verify it, and own the result.
- The ability to go from a question to a production-ready solution.
- The ability to turn complex data into clear recommendations.
- Strong commercial and product judgment, with the ability to balance customer value, monetization, growth, and profitability.
- Experience with pricing, packaging, monetization, or commercial analytics for technical or consumption-based products.
- Strong cross-functional collaboration skills across Product, Engineering, Data, Finance, Sales, and Operations.
- A hands-on and proactive working style, with the ability to operate effectively in an ambiguous and technically complex environment.

Nice to have:

- Familiarity with LLM inference economics: tokens, throughput and latency, batching, GPU costs.

Benefits & Perks:

  • Competitive compensation
  • Career growth and learning opportunities
  • Flexibility and ownership
  • Collaborative and innovative culture
  • Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects
  • International environment and talented teams

What's it like to work at Nebius:

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI

jobs.title: Senior AI/ML Engineer
jobs.jd: This role is also open to candidates living in the EU or EEA. We can't consider applications from other locations. If you've built something before, start here Most ML jobs hand you a benchmark. This one hands you a business problem with paying customers and their real data. Construction tenders are long, messy and full of trade jargon, and every decision a customer makes on our platform becomes a labeled example you can train on. We need someone who can turn that data into models that customers notice: from the first experiment to the model serving production traffic, and back again when a customer says it got something wrong. If you've founded a company (whether it worked out or not), been the first ML engineer somewhere, or shipped a model people paid for, this role was written for you. About Scalera Scalera is an ETH Zurich spin-off building AI for the €200B+ European construction industry. Manufacturers, wholesalers and suppliers in Switzerland, Austria and Germany still run their most document-heavy work by hand, from reading 300-page tenders to retyping purchase orders into their ERP. We automate that work one process at a time, and ML sits at the center of every one of them. What you'll own You'll own the ML behind our products, end to end. In practice that means: Training and fine-tuning : embedding models, rerankers, classifiers and LLMs, trained on our own data. Document understanding : models that pull structure, quantities and product specs out of tenders, orders and catalogs. Product matching : retrieval and LLM agents that match tender positions to the right products. Evaluation : offline benchmarks, per-customer evals and gates that keep a new model from shipping if it makes things worse. Training and serving infrastructure : automated retrain pipelines, GPU serving and vector search in production. Customer problems : when a model gets something wrong for a customer, finding out why and fixing it. What success looks like after 3 months There's a model or part of the pipeline people now think of as yours, and you're the one deciding what happens to it next. You've spotted a problem nobody asked you to solve, made the case for it, and shipped a first version. A model you trained runs in production, and customers can see the difference in their results. Retraining runs automatically, and nothing reaches customers without passing an eval you designed. You've cut LLM cost or latency by replacing an expensive step with a smaller model of your own. You've decided at least one thing we should stop building. You'll probably thrive here if You've taken something from zero to one: a company, a model in production, or a side project with real users. You've trained and fine-tuned models yourself, ideally embeddings, retrieval or document models, and evaluated them honestly on held-out data. You've built with LLMs in production and know where agents fail. You write strong Python and can run what you build: Docker, CI/CD, and cloud on GCP, AWS or Azure. You measure before you believe, and a single aggregate score doesn't convince you. You'd rather open a customer's actual document than wait for a spec. You're comfortable with ambiguity. You can make progress while the problem is still half-defined, which at a startup it usually is. You want a large scope of responsibility and are happy to own things well beyond your job title. Rapidly changing requirements don't throw you. When customers or priorities shift, you adapt and keep going. You enjoy direct customer contact and want to be on customer calls. You write clearly in English. German is a plus, not a requirement. You probably won't enjoy it if You just want to code and go home. You don't like talking to customers. Ambiguity and chaos bother you. You want a well-defined research agenda handed to you. You'd rather hand a model to someone else to deploy and debug. Your main goal is managing people soon. Here, scope grows with what you own, not with headcount. Our stack Python and PyTorch, open-weight and frontier LLMs, LangGraph, Langfuse, PostgreSQL with pgvector, Pinecone, and GCP. You don't need to know all of it on day one. How we hire Screening call (30 min) with our VP Engineering. It's two-way: ask us anything, including the hard questions. Technical deep-dive call : walk us through a model or system you built, the decisions you made and what went wrong in production. Meet Scalera Day : come to our office in Zürich, work on a real problem with real (anonymized) tender data, and meet the team. Offer : if it's a fit on both sides, we'll move quickly to an offer. Working at Scalera Zürich HQ, four days in the office, Fridays remote. If not located in Zürich then this role is open to remote within the EU or EEA, Occasional customer visits across Switzerland, Austria and Germany Small team, no bureaucracy. You'll work directly with the CEO, CTO, VP Engineering and Customer Success Competitive salary and meaningful equity Founders and former founders: if you're unsure whether you fit, send a few lines about what you built and why you moved on. We read every one. Find more English Speaking Jobs in Switzerland on Arbeitnow

jobs.title: Senior Data Scientist, Artist-First AI Music lab
jobs.jd: The Music Mission team owns Spotify 's end to end proposition for music creators and the experiences they create for fans. The team is dedicated to building tools and services to enable creation, promotion, expression, and monetization at scale. We're looking for a Senior Data Scientist to join the Artist-First AI Music lab. Our team explores and advances generative technologies for music to create new experiences for fans and artists, with a focus on listening experiences that center and celebrate artists and creatives. All of our products will put artists and songwriters first, through these four principles: Partnerships with record labels, distributors, and music publishers: We'll develop new products for artists and fans through upfront agreements, not by asking for forgiveness later. Choice in participation: We recognize there's a wide range of views on use of generative music tools within the artistic community. Therefore, artists and rightsholders will choose if and how to participate to ensure the use of AI tools aligns with the values of the people behind the music. Fair compensation and new revenue: We will build products that create wholly new revenue streams for rightsholders, artists, and songwriters, ensuring they are properly compensated for uses of their work and transparently credited for their contributions. We will use our role as the place where more than 700 million people already come to listen to music every month to ensure that generative AI deepens artist-fan connections. For more information, see this press release: https://newsroom.spotify.com/2025-10-16/artist-first-ai-music-spotify-collaboration/ What You'll Do Lead foundational measurement and insights work for generative music experiences, developing the frameworks that help Spotify understand how creators, listeners, and rights holders engage with generative AI music. Design and run large-scale analyses and evaluations of generative music systems, from prompt interpretation to model output quality, using Spotify's unique behavioral datasets, annotations, and experimentation platforms. Ensure donors easily connect with the organizations and causes that matter most to them. Help donors become the best version of themselves by helping them realize their desire to become more consistent in their giving. Own the production reliability and quality of our models. Maximize product goals while minimizing false positives and negative experiences for our giving community. To be successful in this role, you’ll also: Research and prototype computational, statistical, and AI models on real-world donor datasets for various real-world problems. Productize machine learning systems that can generate personalized recommendations for our Donors and help champion their giving journey. Build AI systems that can consume vast amounts of real-time data to a diverse class of problems from Engineering Reliability to Fraud Prevention. Work on a wide array of problems that Machine Learning and AI can be used to solve. Translate ambiguous product problems into well-posed ML formulations. Including ranking, classification, and anomaly detection, with clear success metrics and evaluation design. Build and maintain end-to-end ML pipelines: feature engineering on large datasets, training, evaluation, A/B testing, and deployment. Ship real-time inference services and work with Platform/DevOps on scalability, latency, and monitoring. Mentor engineers on ML best practices and raise the team’s bar for scientific rigor and code quality. Experience with large-scale data processing (Spark, distributed training, feature stores) and modern ML tooling (PyTorch or TensorFlow, scikit-learn, MLflow or similar). Track record in one or more of: recommender systems, fraud/risk modeling, search ranking, or real-time classification. Research background publications, thesis work, or applied research, translating novel methods into shipped solutions, is a strong plus. Your superpowers: Integrity: Demonstrate congruence in thought, speech, and action. Can be trusted to act with courage and to do the right thing. Problem-Solving - Resourceful and creative in solving complex issues. Use sound judgment, data, and collaboration. Scientific rigor: you insist on sound baselines, honest evaluation, and reproducibility. Ownership mindset: you carry models from whiteboard to production and stay accountable for their behavior. Effective Communication - Communicate frequently using clarity and appropriate methods/tools of communication. Customer Focus: Adopting a human-centric approach that meets or anticipates customer needs when developing solutions. Our culture: We are a virtual team of award-winning and high-performing professionals who innovate and collaborate to fulfill our mission to instantly connect people to causes that matter most to them so they can change their world with kindness and generosity. Our four keys to success - integrity, heart, simplicity, and wow - fuel our passion to be recognized among the tech industry’s most inclusive and purpose-driven workplaces. jobs.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer
jobs.jd: Why Faculty? We established Faculty in 2014 because we thought that AI would be the most important technology of our time. Since then, we’ve worked with over 350 global customers to transform their performance through human-centric AI. You can read about our real-world impact here . We don’t chase hype cycles. We innovate, build and deploy responsible AI which moves the needle - and we know a thing or two about doing it well. We bring an unparalleled depth of technical, product and delivery expertise to our clients who span government, finance, retail, energy, life sciences and defence. Our business, and reputation, is growing fast and we’re always on the lookout for individuals who share our intellectual curiosity and desire to build a positive legacy through technology. AI is an epoch-defining technology, join a company where you’ll be empowered to envision its most powerful applications, and to make them happen. About the team Our Public Services Business Unit is committed to leveraging AI for the benefit of individual citizens and the public good. From our work informing strategic government decisions, to optimising our NHS, through to reducing bureaucratic backlogs - we know that AI offers opportunities to drive improvements at every level of Government and we are proud to lead on some of the most impactful work happening in the sector. Because of the nature of the work we do with our Government clients, you may need to be eligible for UK Security Clearance (SC) and willing to work on site with these clients from time to time. About the role As a Senior Machine Learning Engineer, we’ll look to you to lead development and deployment of cutting-edge AI systems for our diverse clients. You’ll design, build, and deploy scalable, production-grade ML software and infrastructure that meets rigorous operational and ethical standards. This is an ambitious, cross-functional role requiring a blend of technical expertise, engineering leadership, and confident client-facing skills. What you'll be doing: Leading technical scoping and architectural decisions for high-impact ML systems Designing and building production-grade ML software, tools, and scalable infrastructure Defining and implementing best practices and standards for deploying machine learning at scale across the business Collaborating with engineers, data scientists, product managers, and commercial teams to solve critical client challenges and leverage opportunities Acting as a trusted technical advisor to customers and partners, translating complex concepts into actionable strategies Mentoring and developing junior engineers, actively shaping our team's engineering culture and technical depth Who we're looking for: You understand the full ML lifecycle and have significant experience operationalising models built with frameworks like TensorFlow or PyTorch You bring deep expertise in software engineering and strong Python skills, focusing on building robust, reusable systems You have demonstrable hands-on experience with cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP), including architecture, security, and infrastructure You've extensive experience working with container and orchestration tools such at Docker & Kubernetes to build and manage applications at scale You thrive in fast-paced, high-growth environments, demonstrating ownership and autonomy in driving projects to completion You communicate exceptionally well, confidently guiding both technical teams and senior, non-technical stakeholders Our Interview Process Talent Team Screen (30 minutes) Pair Programming Interview (90 minutes) System Design Interview (90 minutes) Commercial Interview (60 minutes) #LI-PRIO Our Recruitment Ethos We aim to grow the best team - not the most similar one. We know that diversity of individuals fosters diversity of thought, and that strengthens our principle of seeking truth. And we know from experience that diverse teams deliver better work, relevant to the world in which we live. We’re united by a deep intellectual curiosity and desire to use our abilities for measurable positive impact. We strongly encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, ethnicities, genders, religions and sexual orientations. If you don’t feel you meet all the requirements, but are excited by the role and know you bring some key strengths, please don't hesitate in applying as you might be right for this role, or other roles. We are open to conversations about part-time hours. A note on AI: we're happy for you to use it for research and interview prep, but please don't use it to generate answers during live interviews. We also use an AI note-taker (Metaview) in interviews so interviewers can stay present (which you can opt out of just let us know,) and every application is reviewed by a human, never decided by AI. jobs.title: Data Scientist, Preparedness
jobs.jd: About the Team The Preparedness team is an important part of the Safety Systems https://openai.com/safety/safety-systems org at OpenAI, and is guided by OpenAI’s Preparedness Framework https://openai.com/index/updating-our-preparedness-framework/. Frontier AI models have the potential to benefit all of humanity, but also pose increasingly severe risks. To ensure that AI promotes positive change, the Preparedness team helps us prepare for the development of increasingly capable frontier AI models. This team is tasked with identifying, tracking, and preparing for catastrophic risks related to frontier AI models. The mission of the Preparedness team is to: 1. Closely monitor and predict the evolving capabilities of frontier AI systems, with an eye towards misuse risks whose impact could be catastrophic to our society 2. Ensure we have concrete procedures, infrastructure and partnerships to mitigate these risks and to safely handle the development of powerful AI systems Preparedness tightly connects capability assessment, evaluations, and internal red teaming, and mitigations for frontier models, as well as overall coordination on AGI preparedness. This is fast paced, exciting work that has far reaching importance for the company and for society. About the Role We’re hiring a Data Scientist to help build, evaluate, and continuously improve mitigations that prevent extreme harms from AI systems. This role is for an experienced, highly autonomous individual contributor who can take ambiguous problem statements, structure rigorous analyses, and translate findings into actionable product and policy changes. This position goes beyond “running evals.” You’ll help create mitigation intelligence and monitoring systems that enable OpenAI to detect issues early, measure effectiveness over time, and reduce both over-blocking (unnecessary friction) and under-blocking (missed harm). WHAT YOU’LL DO - Evaluate and improve mitigation systems, including classifiers and detection pipelines across domains (e.g., biosecurity, cybersecurity, and emerging risk areas). - Diagnose false positives and false negatives with deep error analysis, root cause investigation, and clear recommendations for mitigation adjustments. - Build monitoring and measurement frameworks to track mitigation effectiveness over time and across user segments and use cases. - Identify trends in over-blocking vs. under-blocking, quantify customer impact, and propose prioritized interventions. - Develop insights from customer feedback, complaints, and usage patterns to detect shifts in adversarial behavior and system failure modes. - Expand risk monitoring into new areas, including cybersecurity threats and model loss-of-control or sabotage scenarios, in partnership with domain experts. - Communicate results to technical and executive stakeholders with crisp narratives, decision-ready metrics, and clear tradeoffs. You might thrive in this role if you are: - An autonomous operator: you can take a problem statement and independently structure the analysis end-to-end. - Strong at executive-ready communication: concise, clear, and outcome-oriented. - Skilled in turning analysis into productable changes: you’re comfortable influencing across functions to drive mitigation improvements. QUALIFICATIONS - Significant experience in data science or applied analytics in high-stakes domains (e.g., security, trust & safety, abuse prevention, fraud, platform integrity, or reliability). - Strong foundations in experimentation, causal thinking, and/or observational inference; ability to design robust measurement under imperfect data. - Fluency in SQL and Python (or equivalent) for analysis, modeling, and building monitoring workflows. - Experience building metrics, dashboards, and operational monitoring that meaningfully changes outcomes (not just reporting). - Track record of driving cross-functional impact with engineering, product, and research partners. - Cybersecurity data science experience (strong preference), including exposure to threat modeling, adversarial dynamics, abuse patterns, or security telemetry. - Experience with classifier evaluation, calibration, thresholding, and error analysis at scale. Familiarity with detection systems in adversarial settings (e.g., evasion, distribution shift, feedback loops). - Trust & Safety experience is helpful, but not required. - Genuine interest in AI safety, alignment, and catastrophic risk prevention. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement https://cdn.openai.com/policies/eeo-policy-statement.pdf. Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. jobs.title: Applied AI Engineer
jobs.jd: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an Applied AI Engineer based in Switzerland. As an Applied AI Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in designing and building the next generation of intelligent, agentic systems. You will develop the core infrastructure that enables AI agents to manage context, use tools, coordinate tasks, and continuously improve their performance. Working at the intersection of advanced AI research and practical software engineering, you will transform complex operational workflows into reliable, scalable production solutions. You will establish robust evaluation, testing, and observability frameworks to ensure AI-powered systems deliver predictable and measurable results. You will also explore innovative ways to integrate coding agents and specialized subagents into software development processes. Collaborating closely with product and operational teams, you will identify high-impact automation opportunities and translate them into effective technical solutions. As an early core member of the engineering team, you will have significant influence over architectural decisions, technical standards, and the long-term AI strategy. Accountabilities In this role, you will design and implement the technical foundations of agentic systems while driving the adoption of AI-powered engineering workflows. Your responsibilities will include: Design and build essential components of agentic systems, including memory, context management, tool-calling capabilities, orchestration mechanisms, and feedback loops. Develop reusable AI infrastructure that enables new workflows to be introduced quickly, consistently, and with predictable reliability. Build comprehensive evaluation frameworks to measure agent performance, identify failure points, and understand the factors behind successful outcomes. Integrate testing, tracing, debugging, and evaluation into the software engineering lifecycle as fundamental practices. Develop systems and validation processes that allow agentic workflows to be thoroughly assessed before production deployment. Advance the use of large language models (LLMs) in software development by creating sophisticated AI-assisted engineering workflows. Build workflows where coding agents and specialized subagents can explore code repositories, implement changes, review architecture, validate conventions, run evaluations, and iterate with minimal human intervention. Actively use agentic engineering tools and workflows in daily development activities. Design architectures that enable specialized AI agents, tools, deterministic software, and human expertise to work together effectively. Determine when to use LLMs, traditional software solutions, human intervention, or coordinated multi-agent approaches to achieve the best outcomes. Collaborate with operational and product teams to understand existing processes, identify high-value automation opportunities, and transform them into reliable production systems. Establish scalable architectural patterns and engineering standards for agentic systems as the organization grows. Take ownership of technical decisions and contribute to the overall direction of the AI engineering function. Requirements The ideal candidate is a strong software engineer with hands-on experience building production-ready AI systems and the autonomy to solve complex technical challenges in a rapidly evolving environment. The following qualifications and skills are expected: Strong software engineering background, with proven experience independently delivering complex systems from initial concept through production deployment. Practical experience building and deploying AI or agentic systems that have operated in production environments. Demonstrated understanding of real-world AI engineering challenges, including reliability, latency, context management, failure modes, evaluation, and observability. Strong knowledge of agent architectures, tool use, structured outputs, context management, orchestration, evaluation frameworks, and feedback loops. Advanced practical experience with modern LLMs and the ability to build reliable workflows around probabilistic AI systems. Hands-on experience using coding agents and agentic development workflows as part of everyday software engineering. Ability to break down complex engineering tasks across multiple agents or specialized subagents and implement mechanisms for validating and improving their outputs. Strong architectural judgment and the ability to select the right combination of AI models, deterministic software, and human intervention for different challenges. Experience with TypeScript and Node.js, or strong experience developing AI systems in Python combined with the willingness and ability to work in a TypeScript-first environment. High level of autonomy, ownership, and confidence making technical decisions in ambiguous situations. Strong product mindset and the ability to connect engineering decisions with operational efficiency and business outcomes. Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with fluency in English. Startup mentality, including resilience, adaptability, initiative, and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment. Benefits Competitive Compensation: Annual salary ranging from €100,000 to €150,000. Remote Work: Opportunity to work remotely within Europe or the United Kingdom. Early-Team Influence: Join as an early core engineering team member with significant ownership over technical direction and architectural decisions. Technical Autonomy: Shape engineering standards, development practices, tooling, and the foundations of the organization's agentic AI infrastructure. Cutting-Edge Technology: Work extensively with advanced LLMs, autonomous agents, multi-agent architectures, and AI-powered software development workflows. Meaningful Impact: Build production systems that address real oper

jobs.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, AI Safety Evaluations
jobs.location: US, CA, Santa Clara US, Remote
jobs.jd: NVIDIA has helped redefine what computers can do. Now, generative AI is opening new possibilities for how people learn, create, and tackle problems. Realizing that potential means answering some of the hardest questions in AI: Where do models fall short? Which risks are we missing? How do we know our safeguards are working? As an expert in machine learning for Evaluations, you’ll help establish the evidence that guides the next generation of safer AI. Your curiosity and scientific judgment can shape what we test, what we learn, and what we build next. We are looking for a Machine Learning Engineer / AI Researcher / Data Scientist to join our AI Safety and Responsibility efforts within Enterprise Risk Management. Engaging directly in engineering tasks, you will apply your data science and statistics skills. You will turn open research questions into rigorous benchmarks, inventive experiments, and tools that reveal how multimodal large language models behave under pressure. Working with researchers and platform engineers, you’ll connect those discoveries to better training methods and safeguards, with reproducible results that inform technical reviews and executive decisions. If you love asking the question no one has thought to test, and building a convincing way to answer it, come help us define what progress in AI safety looks like. What You Will Be Doing: Safety Benchmarking: Design and maintain safety benchmarks for large language and multimodal models, translating risk scenarios into test cases, datasets, and scoring rubrics. Evaluation Methodology: Define metrics and protocols that assess safety alongside model usefulness, using baselines, uncertainty estimates, and failure analysis to distinguish meaningful improvements from noise. Reproducible Evaluation: Build reusable Python pipelines with versioned datasets, model configurations, and experiment tracking to reproduce results and compare performance across model releases. Automated Red-Teaming: Develop tools to discover failure modes and expand evaluation coverage, incorporating human review to validate automated scoring and provide additional judgment. Failure Analysis: Investigate model failures with researchers, document actionable findings, and develop regression tests to assess whether model changes resolve identified issues. Results and Communication: Partner with platform engineers to store and aggregate evaluation results, and clearly communicate findings, limitations, and emerging risks to researchers and decision-makers. What We Need To See: Education and Experience: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience, with 6+ years in the field of machine learning engineering or evaluation. Evaluation Design: Experience developing benchmarks, metrics, and statistically sound comparisons for ML systems, including selecting baselines and interpreting uncertainty. Ability to translate ambiguous evaluation questions into testable experiments. Engineering: Strong Python skills and experience building maintainable shared tools, data pipelines, and experiment-tracking workflows. Analytical Rigor: Ability to assess dataset quality, identify limitations in metrics and scoring methods, and support conclusions with reproducible evidence. Communication: Clearly explain findings and tradeoffs to researchers, engineering partners, and executives. Ways to Stand Out from the Crowd: Evaluation: Experience evaluating LLMs, multimodal models, or agentic systems through adversarial testing or automated red-teaming. Community Contributions: Contributions to public benchmarks or evaluation frameworks. Research Publications: A publication track record and interest in continuing to publish at top tier venues. jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Agentic Platform - Moveworks
jobs.jd: The Role We're building the runtime infrastructure that powers Moveworks' AI agents — the systems that orchestrate, execute, and deliver agent responses to millions of enterprise users in real time. This role sits where large language models meet distributed systems. You'll apply machine learning, LLM, and distributed systems expertise to make agents plan, reason, and use tools reliably, and you'll build the production systems that run those agents at enterprise scale. Our AI agents can plan, execute multi-step workflows, call tools, wait on human input, and resume — all while maintaining correctness, observability, and low latency. The systems that make this possible are what you'll build and own. What you get to do in this role: Agent orchestration engine — A state machine that manages long-running agent sessions, coordinating planning, execution, and user interaction across multiple LLM calls and tool invocations Model routing and adaptation — Choose, route between, and fine-tune or distill LLMs for specific agent tasks. Meet enterprise requirements such as granular permissions, data freshness, explainability, and preserving general knowledge. Distributed session management — Lease-based ownership using conditional writes, heartbeat protocols, and crash recovery via checkpointing Event-driven message pipeline — FIFO queues for ordered delivery, consumers for event processing, and real-time streaming via gRPC and Socket.IO Structured concurrency — Running multiple concurrent tasks per session with fail-fast semantics and graceful cancellation Observability infrastructure — OpenTelemetry instrumentation, distributed trace context propagation across async boundaries, custom span lifecycle management for sessions that span minutes Caching and state layers — Redis, DynamoDB KV stores with per-org/per-bot scoping, batch read optimization, and hot-reload configuration Tool and agent connectivity for LLMs: Build MCP and agent-to-agent (A2A) capabilities, including tool discovery, namespacing, and tool selection over large tool catalogs, so the LLM picks and calls the right tool from thousands of candidates. Token efficiency and context engineering — Lower the agent's cost and latency through prompt and context discipline, caching, speculative and parallel model-call scheduling, and reducing tokens spent across multi-step LLM reasoning chains. Open-weights model adoption and evaluation — Quickly stand up newly released open-weights LLMs at different quantization levels, run them in a test environment, and benchmark their accuracy, latency and cost on agent tasks. Use the results to decide which models reach production. To be successful in this role you have: You should have deep experience in at least 3 of these areas: Distributed systems: consistency models, idempotency, exactly-once delivery, distributed locking/leasing Concurrent/async programming: Python asyncio, Go goroutines, structured concurrency, cancellation handling Event-driven architectures: message queues (SQS, Kafka), pub/sub, backpressure, delivery guarantees Database systems for infrastructure: DynamoDB (conditional writes, transactions), Redis (connection pooling, pub/sub) Observability: OpenTelemetry, distributed tracing, span context propagation, Prometheus metrics gRPC/protobuf: streaming RPCs, service interface design, error handling patterns Machine learning: Large language models, natural language processing, LLM evaluation Required: 5+ years building production backend/infrastructure systems Strong in Python or Go (ideally both) Experience designing and operating systems that handle real traffic at scale Hands-on experience building production systems that use LLMs or other ML models Comfort with ambiguity — these are novel problems without textbook solutions Relevant past experience: Building and shipping products on large language models with techniques such as RAG, chain-of-thought, self-reflection, tool and function calling, and agentic reasoning. Training, fine-tuning, or evaluating machine learning models on large datasets in production, especially for NLP, retrieval, or ranking. Improving relevance or quality through careful experimentation: designing metrics, building evaluation datasets, and developing new features and signals for ranking or model selection. Research or applied work in machine learning, LLMs, agentic systems, information retrieval, or ranking and relevance.
